turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
My predicted top five are **c038, c030, c044, c088, and c097**. I prioritize candidates that retain a high-performing training stack and make a physically plausible interface modification, rather than assuming that a more elaborate stack is necessarily better.

The training data particularly support **PTAA-based hole contacts with fullerene/buffer electron contacts**, and **appropriately modified NiO contacts**. These combinations can reduce interfacial recombination while maintaining selective extraction. The predictions remain uncertain because layer thickness, processing conditions, and interface treatments are not specified.

| Rank | Candidate | Training evidence and device-physics rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c038** | The closest distinctive analogue—**PCBM-60 / Au-np \| NiO-c / Ag** on FTO—reaches **20.0%**. Au nanoparticles can modify the NiO contact and optical response, although their benefit depends on loading and morphology. c038 retains that promising hole-contact combination and adds **PEI behind PCBM**, where a sufficiently thin dipolar interlayer can improve electron-contact alignment and reduce contact losses. The ITO substrate is also well represented among successful training devices. |
| **2** | **c030** | Its **PCBM-60 \| Bphen / PTAA \| PMMA / Al** backbone directly matches a **19.48%** training configuration. PTAA provides selective hole extraction; a thin PMMA modification can suppress interfacial recombination, while Bphen helps isolate the absorber-side electron contact from Al. The added **IDTT2FPDI** acceptor could improve electron-side coverage or extraction. Crucially, this choice is supported by the strong backbone—not by assuming that the extra acceptor must help. |
| **3** | **c044** | This is a conservative, strong choice: **PCBM-60 \| BCP / PTAA / Cu**. The training set gives **18.85%** for the same materials with an additional C60 layer, and **18.62–19.085%** for related C60/BCP–PTAA–Cu devices. PTAA suppresses electron leakage at the hole contact, PCBM supports electron extraction, and BCP buffers the Cu-facing contact. Omitting C60 may reduce coverage robustness, but the remaining stack is well supported. |
| **4** | **c088** | **C60 \| BCP / PTAA / Cu** is one of the strongest recurring families in the training data, including **19.085%** with slot-die deposition. Doctor blading is independently compatible with this transport-layer family: its Ag-contact analogue reaches **16.9%**. Willow glass should not automatically incur the thermal and dimensional limitations associated with PET, although coating uniformity and ITO resistance introduce uncertainty. |
| **5** | **c097** | The sulfur analogue, **ITCPTC-Th \| C60 \| BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag**, reaches **18.49%** with the same substrate and deposition method. c097 preserves the fullerene/BCP electron-selective contact and P3CT-Na hole contact, changing the molecular acceptor to **ITCPTC-Se**. Selenium substitution can alter polarizability, packing, and electronic levels, making this a credible high-efficiency analogue—but not a guaranteed improvement over the sulfur compound. |

I would not elevate an unfamiliar additive solely because it might passivate defects: poor coverage, an extraction barrier, or excessive insulating-layer thickness can negate that benefit. These five have the strongest combination of high-performing training analogues and plausible selective-contact physics.

**Final: c038, c030, c044, c088, c097**
